grain: one row per campaign_id, plus one campaign_id=NULL 'organic' row

emails_sent.formula: count(email_events where event_type == 'SENT' and campaign_id matches)
caveats: Always 0 for the organic row -- email_events.campaign_id is never null.

emails_opened.formula: count(email_events where event_type == 'OPENED' and campaign_id matches)

emails_clicked.formula: count(email_events where event_type == 'CLICKED' and campaign_id matches)

offers_created.business_definition: Prequalified offers attributed to this campaign (NULL/organic for non-campaign offers).

applications_submitted.business_definition: Applications attributed to this campaign via their offer (organic offer or no-offer application both attribute to the organic row).
applications_submitted.formula: count(applications joined to prequal_offers via offer_id, grouped by the offer's campaign_id)
caveats: Attribution is via offer_id, not a direct campaign_id column on applications -- this is intentional, see context/data_dictionary.json's note on lifecycle_loans not denormalizing campaign attribution.

applications_approved.business_definition: Applications attributed to this campaign whose underwriting decision was APPROVED.
applications_approved.formula: count(underwriting_decisions where decision == 'APPROVED' and the application attributes to this campaign)

loans_funded.business_definition: Loans funded whose originating application attributes to this campaign.
loans_funded.formula: count(loans where the loan's application attributes to this campaign)
caveats: Answers 'which campaign produced the most funded loans?'

open_rate.business_definition: Share of sent emails that were opened.
caveats: Null (not 0) for the organic row and any campaign with zero emails sent -- avoids implying a 0% open rate where there was no denominator.

click_through_rate.business_definition: Share of opened emails that were clicked.

click_to_offer_rate.business_definition: Offers created relative to clicks -- an aggregate-level rate, not a per-click causal trace.
click_to_offer_rate.expected_range: >= 0 or null (can exceed 1 if organic-style repeat offers occur)
caveats: Answers 'what percentage of customers who clicked applied?' at the aggregate level.

offer_to_application_rate.business_definition: Applications submitted relative to offers created.

application_to_approval_rate.business_definition: Applications approved relative to applications submitted.

approval_to_funded_rate.business_definition: Loans funded relative to applications approved (not every approval funds).
